aiHints.empty: Start with one sentence that paraphrases the question.
aiHints.noOverview: Add an overview: begin a sentence with “Overall,”.
aiHints.overview: Overview found. Next: compare the start and end figures.
aiHints.long: Good length. Check your figures, then submit for AI review.

sentences: Many cities have introduced bike lanes.
This has reduced traffic in the centre.
drills.hint: Use “which” after a comma to refer back to the whole first idea.

sentences: Canada had high internet access in 2000.
drills.hint: Put “whereas” between the two contrasting facts, after a comma.

sentences: More firms allow staff to work from home.
drills.hint: Cause first, then the result introduced by “as a result,”.

sentences: The city built new bike lanes.
drills.hint: After the “although” clause and its comma, add the main clause: subject first, then the verb.
Keep the result first, then give the reason with “because”.
“Unless” means “if … not”: the result comes first, then the condition.

lessons.label: Task
lessons.title: Understanding the task
keyPoints: Underline the topic words in the question.
Identify the instruction: agree, discuss, or solve.
Answer every part of the question.

lessons.label: Paraphrase
lessons.title: Paraphrasing the question
keyPoints: Replace key words with accurate synonyms.

lessons.label: Thesis
lessons.title: Writing a thesis
keyPoints: State your opinion in one clear sentence.
Keep the same position until the conclusion.

lessons.label: Intro formula
lessons.title: Writing introductions
keyPoints: Paraphrase the question in one sentence.
Outline the two ideas you will develop.

lessons.label: Conclusions
lessons.title: Writing conclusions
keyPoints: Restate your position with new wording.
Never add a new idea in the conclusion.

lessons.label: Practice
lessons.title: Putting it together
keyPoints: Plan for five minutes before writing.
Write one idea per body paragraph.
Leave three minutes to check your work.

paragraphs.text: Nowadays many people work from home instead of going to the office.
this is good for workers and also for companies, but there are some problems too.
workers do not need to travel, so they save time and money.
companies can pay less for offices…

answers.why: Clear position · relevant main ideas · simple, sometimes repetitive linking · limited range of vocabulary and some grammar errors.

paragraphs.text: In recent years, working from home has become far more common.
it brings real benefits to both employees and employers, although it has some disadvantages.
employees avoid long commutes, which gives them more time for rest.
businesses can reduce the cost of renting office space…

answers.why: Clear position throughout · logical paragraphs with a range of linkers · good vocabulary with some less common words · mostly accurate complex sentences.

modelWhy.task1: Clear overview of the main trends · key features selected and compared with accurate figures · logical paragraphs with varied linking · precise, less common vocabulary for describing change.
modelWhy.task2: Clear position from the first paragraph · each main idea developed with a relevant example · varied, natural linking · precise vocabulary and a wide range of accurate complex sentences.
